title: Endline Comment Repeating the Statement
pattern: An inline comment placed at the end of a line of code that merely restates the statement's direct action.
why_bad: Visual noise and maintenance chore. Endline comments disrupt vertical scanning, require alignment maintenance, and repeat the obvious.
detection: Comments starting with `//` on the same line as a statement, containing only a translation of the code syntax.
counterexample: Short endline annotations carrying non-obvious data, such as units or protocol field names on packed struct fields.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Endline Comments and Their Problems").
